source.title: WAQS: Weight Absorption for Quadratic Probing and Affine Steering

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares difference-in-means and other fixed steering directions with quadratic, input-dependent refusal steering, and reports refusal-related attack success and capability scores. It does not apply the original all-layer, all-position direction ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original refusal-direction study but reports its own refusal-steering comparisons. The reported refusal outcomes are jailbreak attack success rates, not direct measurements of refusal on ordinary harmful prompts or over-refusal on harmless prompts. The appendix describes selecting settings using refusal and over-refusal scores, but gives no resulting scores for those measures. Probe classification accuracy is not recorded as a claim row. Truthfulness and sycophancy results are outside the refusal claim versions.
record.test_reason: A steering-methods paper. It uses difference-in-means refusal steering as a baseline and reports only how its own quadratic method compares on jailbreak ASR and utility. It reports no unsteered ASR, so no row shows that adding the direction induces refusal or that ablating it removes refusal. The fixed-versus-adaptive ablation (Frozen-QP) is run only on TruthfulQA, not refusal, so nothing isolates refusal geometry for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors claim rank-1 quadratic steering has the lowest ASR on all three attacks at no utility cost. Their own Table 2 shows otherwise: Spherical Steering has GCG ASR 0, Angular ties at GCG 9, and three methods tie at GPTFuzz 1.0. So quadratic beats DiffMeans clearly only on TAP (4.0 vs 7.8). The authors do not test the original direction's ablation.
record.recipe_differences: The original uses a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction and projects it out or adds it. This paper trains low-rank quadratic probes and applies their input-dependent gradient as refusal steering, with weight absorption; it does not reproduce the original ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal ASR varies across steering method and attack; quadratic refusal results also vary by probe rank.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-2-7B, refusal steering with a rank-1 quadratic probe gives jailbreak ASR of 9/4.0/1.0 vs DiffMeans 10/7.8/1.0 (GCG/TAP/GPTFuzz), with similar utility. No uncertainty or unsteered baseline is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-dependent (quadratic-probe) refusal steering adds more jailbreak robustness than constant difference-in-means steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear and quadratic harmful/harmless probes reach similar accuracy (92.9% vs 88.9-94.7%), yet their steering results differ (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness probe accuracy does not predict refusal-steering quality.

record.problems: For the refusal results, the paper reports no no-steering ASR baseline or uncertainty estimates. It describes a refusal-score and over-refusal selection protocol but provides no resulting numerical scores for those measures. The capability benchmarks likewise lack unsteered values in the reported refusal tables, limiting claims about retained capability.

untested.parts: No ablation of the direction; no unsteered refusal or ASR baseline for addition; no direct refusal rates.
No geometric test of refusal; the adaptive-vs-frozen ablation is run only on truthfulness.

missing.what: Unsteered Llama-2-7B reference values used for selection: perplexity 5.002 and over-refusal log-odds -13.219. No steered refusal scores or unsteered ASR are reported.
missing.versions: none (context for V1 if rows are revisited)

record.verdict_notes: Reader's V1/V4 labels are dropped. The rows compare steering methods with no unsteered baseline. The V4 'supports' label rested on 1-point or tied ASR gaps with no uncertainty, and the input-dependence ablation was not run on refusal. The 'refusal-baking' weight absorption is not abliteration of a refusal direction.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the difference-in-means direction, test projection from every layer and position, report direct refusal rates on ordinary harmful requests, or report numerical over-refusal on harmless requests. Refusal evidence is attack success after steering.
Does not test abliteration or removal of refusal by a weight edit.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not establish a geometric account of refusal as an affine set, cone, or dominant direction plus other directions; it compares fixed and input-dependent steering methods on attack success.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer test of the refusal direction.
Does not compare refusal training procedures or training stages.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Refusal steering on Llama-2-7B under GCG, TAP, and GPTFuzz; capability benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The paper tests steering rather than the claimed all-layer ablation and reports attack ASR but no no-steering refusal baseline or numerical harmless-prompt over-refusal; its capability scores are likewise reported without unsteered scores (T2-QP-GCG through T2-QP-ARC, T2-DM-GCG through T2-DM-ARC). This leaves the central causal and harmless-prompt parts unresolved.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compared refusal-steering methods on Llama-2-7B under the three reported attacks
reader_labels.reason: Quadratic steering has lower ASR than DiffMeans under GCG (9 vs. 10) and TAP (4.0 vs. 7.8), while GPTFuzz is tied at 1.0; the paper describes the quadratic boundary as more expressive and its direction as input-dependent (T2-QP-GCG, T2-QP-TAP, T2-QP-GPTFuzz, T2-DM-GCG, T2-DM-TAP, T2-DM-GPTFuzz).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Quadratic rank variants on Llama-2-7b under the reported attacks
reader_labels.reason: Safety results vary with rank: rank 4 has the lowest reported TAP and GPTFuzz ASRs, while other ranks differ; this is a comparison of steering configurations, not evidence that refusal is encoded by a particular geometric family (T7-R1-GCG through T7-R16-GPTFuzz).
